name: Question 13
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128542/assets/f370177dc8119044b74fd4923c3d4318d5b9e1b4de89b63967284ee1cd7794da.png)

Consider the rectangular region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ=\{(u,v)\,:\,\sqrt{2}\le u\le 3,\,\,\frac{5\pi }{3}\le v\le \frac{7\pi }{4}\},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v).
$$

Find the image of $Δ$ under the action of $T.$
worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we transform each side of $Δ$ separately:

- Consider the image of the bottom side, where we have $v=\frac{5\pi }{3}$ and $\sqrt{2}\le u\le 3.$ 

Substituting $v=\frac{5\pi }{3}$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y)=(u\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3}),\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3})).\end{aligned}
$$

This line segment makes an angle of $\frac{5\pi }{3}$ with the positive $x$-axis in the $xy$-plane. Moreover, this segment lies on a line that passes through the origin, and its endpoints lie on the circles of radii $\sqrt{2}$ and $3$ centered at $O.$

- Consider the image of the top side, where we have $v=\frac{7\pi }{4}$ and $\sqrt{2}\le u\le 3.$ 

Substituting $v=\frac{7\pi }{4}$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y)=(u\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{4}),\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{4})).\end{aligned}
$$

This line segment makes an angle of $\frac{7\pi }{4}$ with the positive $x$-axis in the $xy$-plane. Moreover, this segment lies on a line that passes through the origin, and its endpoints lie on the circles of radii $\sqrt{2}$ and $3$ centered at $O.$

- Consider the image of the left side, where we have $u=\sqrt{2}$ and $\frac{5\pi }{3}\le v\le \frac{7\pi }{4}.$ 

Substituting $u=\sqrt{2}$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y)=(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v).\end{aligned}
$$

This is an arc of the circle of radius $\sqrt{2}$ centered at the origin in the $xy$-plane. The arc lies in the first quadrant between the polar rays $\theta =\frac{5\pi }{3}$ and $\theta =\frac{7\pi }{4}.$

- Consider the image of the right side, where we have $u=3$ and $\frac{5\pi }{3}\le v\le \frac{7\pi }{4}.$ 

Substituting $u=3$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y)=(3\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡v).\end{aligned}
$$

This is an arc of the circle of radius $3$ centered at the origin in the $xy$-plane. The arc lies in the first quadrant between the polar rays $\theta =\frac{5\pi }{3}$ and $\theta =\frac{7\pi }{4}.$

Therefore, the image $D$ of $Δ$ under the action of $T$ is the region that is enclosed between 

- two circles with polar equations $r=\sqrt{2}$ and $r=3,$ and

- two rays with polar equations $\theta =\frac{5\pi }{3}$ and $\theta =\frac{7\pi }{4},$

as shown in the diagram below.

and the transformation T, given by T:(u,v)→(ucos⁡v,usin⁡v).

Find the image of Δ under the action of T.

EXPLANATION

To map the entire region Δ onto the xy-plane, we transform each side of Δ separately:

  • Consider the image of the bottom side, where we have v=5π3 and 2≤u≤3.

    Substituting v=5π3 into our transformation equations, we obtain (x,y)=(ucos⁡(5π3),usin⁡(5π3)). This line segment makes an angle of 5π3 with the positive x-axis in the xy-plane. Moreover, this segment lies on a line that passes through the origin, and its endpoints lie on the circles of radii 2 and 3 centered at O.

  • Consider the image of the top side, where we have v=7π4 and 2≤u≤3.

    Substituting v=7π4 into our transformation equations, we obtain (x,y)=(ucos⁡(7π4),usin⁡(7π4)). This line segment makes an angle of 7π4 with the positive x-axis in the xy-plane. Moreover, this segment lies on a line that passes through the origin, and its endpoints lie on the circles of radii 2 and 3 centered at O.

  • Consider the image of the left side, where we have u=2 and 5π3≤v≤7π4.

    Substituting u=2 into our transformation equations, we obtain (x,y)=(2cos⁡v,2sin⁡v). This is an arc of the circle of radius 2 centered at the origin in the xy-plane. The arc lies in the first quadrant between the polar rays θ=5π3 and θ=7π4.

  • Consider the image of the right side, where we have u=3 and 5π3≤v≤7π4.

    Substituting u=3 into our transformation equations, we obtain (x,y)=(3cos⁡v,3sin⁡v). This is an arc of the circle of radius 3 centered at the origin in the xy-plane. The arc lies in the first quadrant between the polar rays θ=5π3 and θ=7π4.

Therefore, the image D of Δ under the action of T is the region that is enclosed between

  • two circles with polar equations r=2 and r=3, and

  • two rays with polar equations θ=5π3 and θ=7π4,

as shown in the diagram below.
